paper_metadata.title: Federated Learning in Quantum Computing for Privacy-Preserving and Distributed Quantum Model Training

summary: The paper proposes a simulated Privacy‑Preserving Quantum Federated Learning (PQFL) framework using parameterized quantum circuits with QHE and QDP. In hybrid simulations, centralized QML achieved 91.4% accuracy, PQFL without QDP 90.1%, and PQFL with QDP 88.7% with privacy budget ε=1.2; communication overhead increased from 850 KB (centralized) to 920–960 KB for PQFL while qubit utilization decreased slightly from 75% to 70–72%.

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical federated learning framework (PQFL) for privacy-preserving distributed training of parameterized quantum models, evaluated against centralized QML and PQFL variants with/without quantum differential privacy.

algorithm.variant: Privacy-Preserving Quantum Federated Learning (PQFL) with parameterized quantum circuits, quantum homomorphic encryption, and quantum differential privacy

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Input data are encoded into quantum states using a feature encoding circuit; the paper mentions angle encoding and amplitude encoding as examples, but does not specify which was used in the experiments.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize mean squared error between predicted and true labels for binary classification in a federated quantum model training setting.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Quantum homomorphic encryption for secure aggregation; quantum differential privacy via additive quantum noise channels before encryption.

problem_instance.description: Federated training of quantum machine learning models across multiple clients with privacy-preserving secure aggregation.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Local client datasets are encoded into quantum states; no dataset-specific preprocessing details are reported.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparison of three configurations: centralized QML, PQFL without QDP, and PQFL with QDP; metrics reported are accuracy, privacy loss (epsilon), communication overhead, and qubit utilization.

noise_model.noise_type: quantum differential privacy noise channels (quantum Gaussian noise / depolarizing or Pauli noise)

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Local training on client-held data; parameter-shift gradient estimation; encrypted aggregation via QHE.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Decryption of aggregated ciphertext by clients; averaging of decrypted updates to form the next global model.

speedup_claims.caveats: No explicit speedup claim or runtime comparison is reported; the paper only provides comparative accuracy, privacy loss, communication overhead, and qubit utilization.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not discussed; paper provides no asymptotic complexity, qubit scaling, or runtime comparison against classical ML methods.
limiting_factors: No real QPU experiments; evaluation done in hybrid simulation.
Dataset, feature dimension, and circuit size are not specified.
No runtime or scaling comparison with classical ML baselines.
No complexity analysis or theoretical speedup claim.
Quantum circuits used only as components of a privacy-preserving federated learning framework.

notes: No specific QPU or device is named; implementation is described as hybrid quantum-classical simulation using Qiskit, PennyLane, and TensorFlow Quantum, so hardware.type is inferred as simulator_other.
The paper reports qubit utilization percentages (75%, 72%, 70%) but does not state an absolute qubit count, so num_qubits remains null.
The paper describes parameterized quantum circuits and parameter-shift gradients but does not report explicit circuit depth or layer count; no exact depth can be extracted.
